events.text: You wake and someone you love is sitting at the end of the bed, saying good morning. You know the face. You know the voice, the laugh, the way they take their tea. You open your mouth to say their name, and there is nothing there. Not forgotten the way a word is forgotten: gone, like a tooth. On the pillow is a single black thread you did not put there.

effects.log: It is cold as river ice and smells of incense. Somewhere, someone is eating names. (The Forgotten Names, in the Jianghu)

choices.text: Say "good morning" back, and hide it

effects.log: You say good morning. You do not say the name. Nobody notices yet. (The Forgotten Names, in the Jianghu)

events.text: Last night you read the last page of the black-bound manual you bought from a pedlar who would not give his own name. This morning you cannot give anyone theirs. Your family stands around you, worried, calling you by your name, and you can only look from face to face and say: you, and you, and you.

effects.log: You throw it in the stove. It will not burn. That is the first clue. (The Forgotten Names, in the Jianghu)

choices.text: Write the faces down, so you do not lose those too

effects.log: You draw them all, badly, and write under each: someone I love. (The Forgotten Names, in the Jianghu)

events.text: The breakthrough went wrong in the night: the qi ran backwards through the memory palace and scoured it like a flood. In the morning your body is whole, your realm is whole, your arts are whole. It is only that the people you love have become someone, someone, and someone.

choices.text: Go back into seclusion to look for the damage

effects.log: You find it: a palace of rooms, every door still there, every nameplate washed blank. (The Forgotten Names, in the Jianghu)

choices.text: Go out and spend the day with them anyway

effects.log: They do not need you to say their names to be glad you are here. It helps less than it should. (The Forgotten Names, in the Jianghu)

events.text: The one you married has started leaving little notes around the house, in a careful hand: on the teapot, on the door, on the pillow. Each one says the same name. Each one you read, and the name slides off your eyes like water off oiled paper, and you see someone looking at you hopefully from the doorway.

effects.log: You keep them all in a box. One day you will be able to read them.

choices.text: Tell the truth: it slides away

effects.log: You say it. Someone sits down with you and holds your hand, and does not leave notes any more, and does not let go.

events.text: A child of yours calls you from across the yard and you turn and smile and cannot answer with a name. The child stops running halfway to you. "You forgot again," the child says, not angry, only trying to understand a grown-up thing.

effects.log: "Just not my name," says the child. "That is all right. I know yours."

choices.text: Make up a pet name for now

effects.log: You call the child Little Sparrow. The child decides that is a fine name to be going on with.

events.text: An old friend visits and you greet them with a warm, blank "you". Their smile stays where it is, but something behind it steps back. On the way out they say, to nobody: "Maybe I was never very important." You hear it.

effects.log: You catch up at the gate. "You are important," you say. "It is the curse, not you." Someone nods, and believes you, a little.
A long letter, addressed to "my friend, whose name a curse has taken". The reply comes in a week. It is longer.

events.text: The black thread from your pillow leads, after a year of asking, to a teahouse in the demonic quarter where an old woman tells you a name for a price: Mo Sangwol, the Name-Eater, who sews names into threads and eats them, and grows younger every time. He takes the names of the well-loved, she says. They taste better.

effects.log: She pockets it. "He lives above a dyer's shop," she says. "For now." (First clue)

choices.text: Ask how many names he has eaten

effects.log: "Enough to make a very long life," she says.

events.text: A librarian of the old sect archives turns pale at the description of the black-bound manual. "The Book of Clean Rooms," he whispers. "It was written by a master who wanted to forget a grief, and it forgets everything that grief was ever attached to. It was banned three hundred years ago. It should not exist."

choices.text: Ask how the master was cured

effects.log: "He was not," says the librarian. "But his student wrote how it might be done." He goes to look. (First clue)

choices.text: Ask who might sell such a thing

effects.log: The librarian will not say. His face says enough.

events.text: A physician of the inner arts listens to your meridians for an hour and finally nods. "The memory palace is washed, not burned," she says. "The rooms are there. The nameplates are blank. Washed things can be inked again, with the right medicine."

effects.log: "The Lotus of Returning," she says. "It grows where people go to remember." (First clue)
"As long as you like," she says. "It does not get worse. It only stays."

events.text: The second thread is untangled. You know now how this thing could be undone: where the curse lives, and how to reach it, and what it fears. You sit up half the night writing it all down, in case you forget that too.

effects.log: It holds. Your own handwriting is the one thing the curse cannot take. (Second clue)

choices.text: Show it to someone you love

effects.log: Someone reads it twice and says: "Then let us do it." (Second clue)

events.text: The last piece: the cost. Whatever breaks the curse will take something from you, a fight, a seclusion, a fortune. And even then, the old records say, the deepest names, the ones most dear, will not come back at once. They will have to be found again, one by one, in the company of each person. And the names of the dead will not come back at all.

effects.log: It is a price. You will pay it. (Last clue: the cure can be tried)

choices.text: Grieve for the dead names first

effects.log: You sit with the list of the dead you can no longer name. Then you get up. (Last clue: the cure can be tried)

events.text: A year of letters, archives, teahouses and rumours, and the thread runs out in your hands. Somewhere out there is the answer. It is not here.

effects.log: You start a new page. The old pages go in the box with the notes.

choices.text: Spend the evening with the people you love instead

effects.log: You cannot say their names. You can still make them laugh.

events.text: Mo Sangwol's room above the dyer's shop is hung with black threads, thousands of them, each one a name. When the Name-Eater falls, the threads go slack all at once, and from far across the city, faint as bells in fog, the names come home.

effects.log: You cut them all. Somewhere in the city, a hundred other people sit up in bed and say a name aloud.

choices.text: Find your own threads and keep them

effects.log: You find your own, tied with a little red knot. You keep them in the box with the notes.

events.text: It breaks. The rooms of the memory palace are inked again, nameplate by nameplate, and you walk through them saying names aloud like a child learning to read. Most of them come. A few doors stay blank, and you know why: those are the dearest, and they will come only with their people.

effects.log: At home, faces turn to you, and you say their names, one after another, and some of them weep.

choices.text: Sit with the blank doors a while

effects.log: You sit with them. You know whose they are. You will open them one by one.

events.text: Not this time. The cure slips through your fingers, and the names stay where they are, on the far side of a wall you can see through but not walk through. You go home. Someone has kept dinner warm.

effects.log: You eat. You plan. The curse has all the time in the world. So, you decide, do you.

choices.text: Tell someone how close it was

effects.log: "Close is something," says someone. "Close is a start."

events.text: You spend the whole day together, the way you used to: the market, the river, the long walk home. Nothing happens. Then at the gate, in the evening light, they turn to say goodnight, and the name is simply there in your mouth, as if it had only stepped out for a while. "{nc_name}," you say. They stop, and turn, and cannot speak.

effects.log: "{nc_name}." It sounds like the best word you know. It is.
You hold on. Neither of you says anything for a long time, because you do not need to.

events.text: It comes back in the middle of something ordinary: they are teaching you a song you once taught them, and they get a line wrong, and you correct it, and the name comes with the line. "{nc_name}, it goes up at the end." You both stop singing.

effects.log: You finish it together. It goes up at the end.
You laugh until you are both crying, over a song.

events.text: The names are back, most of them. But there are faces in your memory that the curse took while their people were still alive, and those people have died since, unnamed. You stand at their graves and read the names carved there, and the names slide off the stone like water. Those will not come back in this life.

choices.text: Burn incense for someone, and someone

effects.log: You burn incense for each of them. You do not need their names to grieve them.

choices.text: Ask the living to tell you about them

effects.log: They tell you stories. The names stay gone. The stories stay.

events.text: Twelve years now. You have learned to live inside it: you know your people by their laughs, their walks, the way they take their tea. Someone and someone and someone, and every one of them dear. It is not a cure. It is a kind of peace.

choices.text: Keep looking for the cure anyway

effects.log: You keep the box of notes by the bed. One day.
You stop counting the years. The people you love do not mind what you call them.

events.text: You have a habit nobody understands: you write down the name of everyone you love, every new year, on a fresh sheet of paper, and read it aloud. People tease you about it. You do not stop. Somewhere in your soul is a box of notes that you never want to need again.

effects.log: Every name comes. Every one. You sit with that a while.

choices.text: Add a new name this year

effects.log: There is a new name on the list. You say it three times, to be sure.

events.text: When someone tells you their name you hold on to it like a coin in a fist, and say it back, always. "You are very careful with names," people say. You do not know why. Your soul remembers a life where it lived among someones.

effects.log: They smile. Most people are not used to being remembered so carefully.
Every name means something. You collect the meanings as other people collect stamps.
